no_ladder.description: Why no judged question is written, or null: the topic has no main figure or event (none, or several with none the main one); nothing in it can be checked on a date (for an event: no date given and no period named, unless it is a pending regulatory decision, which is due at the company's current fiscal year-end); a company's figure for a quarter or a half-year; a figure for a year that has already ended on the item's day; a figure for a year beyond next year (unless the topic's opens_as is binding_obligation); or the question belongs to another company or to a matter no listed theme covers (name it). Exactly one of no_ladder and ladder is null (checked by code).

question.description: The one judged question: one figure for a named period, or one event. For a figure it names the period covered or the day measured at, and the material that settles it. It stands on its own for a reader who never sees this item.

object.description: The company's ticker, or a theme id from the themes listed in the request. Nothing else: a question with another object is returned as no_ladder.

not_judged.description: Every other part of the topic's wording that the question leaves out (a second figure or event, a condition, a comparison); empty only when the question leaves nothing of the wording out.

yes_no.description: For an event that happens or not by the due day; else null. Exactly one of yes_no, company_states, theme_states and figure is not null (checked by code).

yes.description: The condition under which the answer is Yes: the event has happened by the due day.

no.description: The condition under which the answer is No.

company_states.description: For the company's event that can end in more than two states: exactly five states; else null.

label.description: Each label used once, meaning good or bad for the business.

theme_states.description: For a theme's event that can end in more than two states: exactly five states; else null.

name.description: A short name of the state itself; each name different.

figure.description: For one figure: its unit, the year it covers, exactly five ranges and, for a company, the favourable end; else null.

unit.description: other when the unit is none of the listed; the question then names it.

year.description: The one year the figure covers: FY2027 for a company's figure (its fiscal year); 2026 for a theme's figure (a calendar year). Code refuses the other form.

lo.description: Inclusive lower bound, a number; null for the lowest range only.

hi.description: Exclusive upper bound, a number; null for the highest range only.

favourable_end.description: For a company's figure: higher or lower, the end that is good for its business (n/a is refused). For a theme's figure: n/a (higher or lower is refused).

favourable_why.description: For a company's figure: one sentence on why that end is good for the business; it may not be empty. For a theme's figure: empty.

words.description: One unbroken passage copied from the item exactly, stating what the market expects: a consensus, the company's guidance, the stated plan or deadline. Not reworded, not reordered, not the topic's wording.

value.description: The number the item states for it, in the figure's unit. Null when the item gives the expectation in words alone, and for an event's reference that is not a number. Never a number the item does not state.

due_day_basis.description: For a figure: stated or expected_publication. For an event: stated, or period_end (the last day of the period the topic names, or the company's current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision with no date).
